newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strikes disrupt French trains, threaten Air France.
newsitem.headline: Strikes disrupt French trains, threaten Air France.

text.p: Striking French train controllers disrupted rail services for a second day on Thursday, while pilots at state-owned airlines Air France and Air Inter Europe voted to walk out for four days from next Tuesday.
The SNCF state-run railway authority said there were fewer train services on Thursday than on Wednesday, the first day of the three-day action.
Labour unions were threatening to extend the strike into the weekend, SNCF said.
High-speed trains between Paris and Brussels and Eurostar trains connecting London to Paris and Brussels through the Channel tunnel were unaffected.
But services were cut by about a third on other high-speed TGV and regional lines across France, SNCF said.

Separately, six pilots' unions at Air France and its short-hop affiliate Air Inter Europe, formerly Air Inter, announced their intention to resume next Tuesday a strike begun last month after talks with management broke down.
The strike is to protest against planned wage cuts and changes in working conditions under a merger between the European airline and its international parent.

The stoppage could cost the group 400 million francs ($70.1 million), an Air France spokeswoman said. "The cost of a strike involving the cancellation of all flights is estimated at 100 million francs a day," she said.
The pilots decided to renew the strike after talks on Wednesday ended in complete disagreement, a union official said.

The Air France group decided on Thursday to postpone any decision on pilots' work conditions until the end of June and called on the unions to take advantage of the time to discuss the issue and other matters, the company said in a statement.
The train controllers, who staged a 48-hour stoppage last month, are protesting against planned job cuts on regional routes and demanding negotiations on bonuses.

SNCF management has said it was willing to pursue negotiations opened several weeks ago, but it could not improve its terms because of financial constraints and the need to preserve fairness among the company's staff. ($ = 5.705 French Francs)
